items.prompt: Ahmet hastaymış. What does the speaker mean?
options: Ahmet is sick, apparently — someone told me
I saw for myself that Ahmet was sick
items.explanation: -ymış is hearsay or discovery: “turns out,” “they say.” The speaker never saw Ahmet sick.

items.prompt: Kafe kapalıydı. How does the speaker know?
options: was at the café and saw it
items.explanation: -ydı is the witness voice: I was there, I saw it. If he’d read it, he’d say kapalıymış.
Last vowel e, so -miş. It ends in a consonant, so no y.

items.prompt: How do you say “Turns out the museum isn’t open today”?
items.explanation: “Not open” is değil: değil + miş = değilmiş. Yok is about things that aren’t there. Değildi means I saw it myself.

items.translation: The weather is great, turns out.
items.explanation: Last vowel e → -miş. Ends in the consonant l, no y.

items.translation: They say Ahmet is very tired.
items.explanation: Last vowel u → -muş.

items.translation: This house is really big, turns out.
items.explanation: Last vowel ü → -müş.

items.translation: Turns out Ahmet is sick, he won’t come today.
items.explanation: Hasta ends in the vowel a: first y, then -mış. Hastaymış.

items.translation: They say the café has no Wi-Fi.
items.explanation: “There isn’t any” is yok. Yok + muş = yokmuş: last vowel o.

entries.text: Walked up to the café: lock on the door
Read in the app: the café is closed
Went to the concert yesterday: it was great
Pushed the door — it’s not locked!
Rode in this taxi myself: it was clean

items.explanation: Were there and saw it — -ydı. Heard it, read it, or just now discovered it — -ymış.

items.translation: Turns out Ahmet is sick, he won’t come today.
items.explanation: Timur didn’t see Ahmet, he got a text. So it’s hastaymış, not hastaydı.
Meğer means “turns out.” About yourself: yorgun + muş + um = yorgunmuşum.

items.prompt: Tap the word with the mistake
items.explanation: Hasta ends in a vowel, so you need y: hastaymış.

items.prompt: Tap the word with the mistake
items.explanation: In English, “I” is enough. In Turkish the ending says who: yorgun + muş + um. Ben alone doesn’t do it.

exercises.instruction: Push notifications: pass each one on correctly
exercises.description: Notifications in the rota taxi. Eye — Timur saw it himself, message — someone told him. Pick the form.

items.explanation: Read it in the app — hearsay: kapalıymış.
Rode it and saw it — witness: uzundu.
A friend told her — hearsay. Last vowel e: güzelmiş.
It was in a review — yokmuş. O → -muş.
Surprise: just discovered it — açıkmış.
A discovery about yourself: yorgun + muş + um.

items.prompt: How do you say “They say this restaurant is expensive”?
items.explanation: They say — that’s hearsay: -ymış. Pahalı ends in a vowel, so you need y.
Öğretmen + miş + sin: a discovery about the person you’re talking to.

items.statement: If you saw for yourself that the café was closed, it’s better to say “Kafe kapalıymış.”
items.explanation: You saw it yourself — that’s the witness: Kafe kapalıydı.

items.prompt: “Apparently, the café was closed yesterday.” In Turkish?
items.explanation: English “was” doesn’t mean -dı. You didn’t see it, so -mış — it works for the past too: kapalıymış.

items.prompt: Otelde havuz ___. Turns out the hotel has no pool.
items.explanation: There isn’t any — yok. You found out, didn’t see — yokmuş.
